hints: Differentiate twice and set the result to zero.
worded:
1. v = 2at − 3bt², and a(t) = 2a − 6bt.

2. Acceleration starts positive (2a) and falls linearly; it is zero when 6bt = 2a, i.e. t = a/3b. (C)

3. Option (B), 2a/3b, is where the velocity is zero, not the acceleration.
mistakes: Setting v = 0 gives t = 2a/3b (option B): that’s when the particle turns round, not when a = 0.
